sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Big discovery: from the left anchor (33,18)-(44,24), DOWN → (34,27)-(43,36) — that's the position of the bottom block! The active block moved to where the bottom block is! Wait — (34,27,43,36) is exactly the bounding box of the bottom block. So does that mean the active block swapped positions with the bottom block?? Or did the active block move to the bottom block's position (overlapping)?
Wait, in my anchor() function I'm looking for a W node with 60<pixels<120. The bottom block has 100 pixels. If the active block moved to the bottom block's position, the two would overlap and merge into a single node (same color W, connected) — in that case the pixel count should be about 184, which wouldn't match 60-120. But the result was (34,27,43,36) with pixels in the 60-120 range… hmm, wait, I'm not printing the pixel count. Let me check: if they merged, the node would be 184 pixels and anchor() would return None. It returned (34,27,43,36), so there exists a W node of 60-120 pixels at the bottom block's position.
Oh wait. Maybe the active block swapped with the bottom block! The active block is now at the bottom block's position (34,27)-(43,36), and the bottom block is now at the left anchor's position (33,18)-(44,24)? Let me check: in the image, the framed block is on the left (vertically elongated), and the plain block is on the right. Hmm, in the current image the frame is still on the left block. Wait, the image shows the framed vertically-elongated block on the left, and the plain square on the right — same as before. But that's the current frame after the restoration… the last probe was RIGHT (restoration from LEFT), and the state is at the left anchor.
Hmm wait, but the DOWN probe: the active block moved to (34,27)-(43,36)?? And then the UP restoration brought it back to (33,18)-(44,24). But wait — if the active block moved to the bottom block's position, what happened to the bottom block? Did they swap? If they swapped, then after the UP restoration… the active block is back at the left anchor, and the bottom block is back at (34,27)-(43,36).
Wait a moment, but actually — maybe DOWN from the left anchor doesn't move the active block; maybe it activates the bottom block (the frame moves to the bottom block)! The "anchor" I detected at (34,27,43,36) might be the bottom block with the frame on it — but the frame is gray, and the bottom block is white with 100 pixels. My anchor() finds a W node of 60-120 pixels: the bottom block itself is 100 pixels at (34,27,43,36)! So when the active block moved somewhere (or the frame moved to the bottom block), anchor() found the bottom block instead.
I need to distinguish: which block has the frame (gray border)? Let me look at the actual frame during the DOWN probe. I'll redo the probe, but this time capture the full state (all W and g nodes) after DOWN.

sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def full(f):
    out=[]
    for n in f.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color'] in ('W','p','g') and n['pixels']>20:
            b=n['boundary']; rows=[p[0] for p in b]; cols=[p[1] for p in b]
            out.append((n['color'],n['pixels'],min(rows),min(cols),max(rows),max(cols)))
    return out
print("before:", full(current_frame))
action(['DOWN'])
print("after DOWN:", full(current_frame))
action(['UP'])
print("restored:", full(current_frame))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
